name: Ukraine

what: Full-scale invasion, now a grinding war of attrition

how: Daily drone, missile and artillery strikes along a front over 1,100 km long
current: Russia has continued its nightly attacks on Ukraine, with missiles targeting Kyiv and hitting bridges, resulting in deaths and damage. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that the Russian attack included 400 drones and over 110 missiles. The situation remains escalated with ongoing violence and failed talks.

name: Gaza
what: War technically under ceasefire, but violence continues
when: War since Oct 7, 2023; ceasefire since Oct 10, 2025
how: Over 1,300 people killed since the "ceasefire" began; disarmament and reconstruction stalled
current: Israel launched a new ground offensive in central Gaza on 18 Nov, pushing tanks west of the “Yellow Line” and issuing forced‑evacuation orders, which regional outlets describe as a breach of the ceasefire. The operation ended the next day, with Gazans returning to assess damage, while humanitarian groups report mass displacement and dire conditions.

sources.label: Al Jazeera: What does Israel’s new ground offensive mean for Palestinians in Gaza?
DW: Israel starts new Gaza ground operation against Hamas
AFP: Gazans return after Israel army ends rare ground operation
Al Jazeera: Families flee Gaza’s Bureij camp as Israel launches new offensive

perspective.dominant_frame: Tier 1 (AFP) reports the operational timeline, noting the offensive began on 18 Nov and ended on 19 Nov with residents returning. Tier 3 outlets (Al Jazeera, DW) stress the humanitarian impact, describing forced evacuations, displacement and a violation of the ceasefire. Together they frame the event as a brief but intense escalation with serious civilian consequences.

escalation.note: New ground offensive launched 18 Nov, mass displacement, operation ended 19 Nov

name: Iran
who: Israel and the US vs Iran
what: A leadership-shattering war, now in an uneasy pause
how: US-Israeli strikes killed Iran’s Supreme Leader; his son succeeded him; Hormuz still shut
current: The United States and Iran have resumed a cycle of tit‑for‑tat strikes, with Iran launching drone attacks on U.S. radar and air‑defence sites in Bahrain and Kuwait, and the U.S. responding with strikes on Iranian missile launch sites. President Trump has postponed any decision on a larger U.S. strike until 2027, saying the United States will “see what happens” after Jan. 1, while Iran continues to target commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

sources.label: AP News: Iranian drone attack targets US radar facility in Bahrain
BBC News: US‑Israel war with Iran
The New York Times: Trump Weighs New Strikes on Iran as Israel Presses for Action, Officials Say

perspective.dominant_frame: Tier‑1 outlets (AP, BBC, NYT, Reuters) frame the situation as an escalating military exchange and a U.S. political calculation to delay further strikes, while Tier‑3 regional outlets add detail on shipping attacks and diplomatic deadlock. All sources agree the conflict is intensifying.

escalation.note: Continued drone attacks on Bahrain/Kuwait and US strike delay keep escalation high

Sudan and Ethiopia are trading accusations of supporting armed groups, and tensions between them are escalating.

name: Myanmar

what: Civil war following the 2021 coup, now with a civilian facade

how: Junta-backed party swept a sham election; war with resistance forces continues in the borderlands

A recent airstrike on a displacement camp in Rakhine state killed 12 people, including a five-year-old child, and wounded 18 others. The International Court of Justice has found Myanmar guilty of genocide against the Rohingya, with evidence showing that Myanmar forces killed at least 10,000 Rohingya.

Regional tensions have risen as Kinshasa threatens to leave the Francophonie over accusations that Rwanda backs the M23 rebel group.
